title: Lane-stripe render consumes flow.lane_caps, which this same diff proves is one tick stale after a fast-path edit — stripes and the HUD readout can disagree transiently
evidence:
+			if int(ps) < len(flow.lane_caps) {
+				c := flow.lane_caps[ps]

+			// (NOT flow.lane_caps: a fast-path edit this frame has not been
+			// stepped yet, so the flow buffer would be one frame stale; the

+			caps := pp.qos_pipe_caps(&app.state.topology, &app.cat, ps, u32(app.sel_pipe))
detail: A right-click dial edit applies weights immediately but lane_caps rebuilds only at the next flow_step; draw_bundles sums flow.lane_caps while the same frame's readout uses fresh qos_pipe_caps — stripes show old proportions until the next tick.
recommended_fix: Have draw_bundles consume the fresh qos_pipe_caps path (or a rebuilt-flag) so stripes and readout agree on the frame an edit lands.

title: intent_apply_tick_raw re-implements the tick math instead of reusing intent_apply_tick; the documented fixed-group-order guarantee holds only while the two procs stay identical
detail: A second, separately-named tick-conversion proc beside the existing intent_apply_tick is either dead duplication or silently divergent math; if the procs differ, same-tick draw/demolish vs emphasis/lane directives land on different ticks and the documented "always beats" ordering is not guaranteed.
recommended_fix: Route emphasis/lane lowering through intent_apply_tick (or make _raw call it) so one proc owns the math, and pin identical results with a harness test.

title: Rejection toast renders only while a pipe is selected, but right-click cycling acts on any hit pipe — a rejected dial move on an unselected pipe is silent
location: app/main.odin (draw_hud toast block + cycle_emphasis + right-click handler)
evidence:
+	} else {
+		// a rejected dial move is never silent (e.g. E6's never-drop zeroing
+		// guard once never-drop content exists) — surface it in the HUD.

+		if app.last_reject != .None && app.tick - app.reject_tick < 30 { // ~1.5s at 20Hz
+			draw_text(app, reject_label(app.last_reject), 12, 156, 16, rl.Color{200, 60, 60, 255})

+		if pid, ok := pipe_hit(app, wx, wy); ok {
+			cycle_emphasis(app, pid)
detail: The toast block sits inside `if app.sel_pipe >= 0`, yet the right-click path cycles the hit pipe without selecting it (left-click selects). An E6 rejection there sets last_reject but no toast draws — contradicting the code's own "never silent" comment.
recommended_fix: Draw the toast outside the sel_pipe guard, or have right-click select the pipe before cycling.
